spells.canonAnchor: heat is the working currency of a crafting - Gerik knits skin shut with 'heat energy from the enemies' (L445); Eric links a campfire to refill himself (L505)
spells.provenance: Simple Magic seed spell, the TEMPERATURE axis. 1.5 degrees of held warmth for ten minutes of ward time - a dry coat on a wet quay, nothing more. SELF because no link needs forging to your own hands.

spells.canonAnchor: the same transfer across a bridged link - 'a crafting requires a link between the two entities, normally this would be an arm or a blade' (L459)
spells.provenance: Simple Magic seed spell. Warm the Hands with one word changed (SELF -> TOUCH) and a little more difficulty for the link it now has to open: the target shape is data too.

spells.canonAnchor: the same transfer with the endpoint swapped: an emptied chromatis stake reads 'very cold to the touch, almost like ice' (L2782-2784)
spells.provenance: Simple Magic seed spell. Proof the axes are signed rather than paired: this is Warm the Hands with a minus sign and nothing else. Keeps a catch from turning on a hot day.

spells.canonAnchor: 'too much energy hurts... you're applying it to a small part of his body' (L448)
spells.provenance: Simple Magic seed spell, the HARM axis at its floor. One hit point, once - a nettle-snap, the smallest transfer a link can carry. No crafting on the public shelf can put a body on the ground; the vitality floor is structural (ActiveEffects.VITALITY_FLOOR).

spells.canonAnchor: 'it would be less taxing to do lots of tiny transfers than one big one' (L457); energy into a body concentrates and hurts (L448-449)
spells.provenance: Simple Magic seed spell. A trickle, not a blow: three doses of one hit point as the heat works through. Deliberately dearer than Sting because the cost model prices every dose it will deliver.

spells.canonAnchor: Gerik heals his own arm by 'knitting the skin back together with heat energy from the enemies' (L445) - canon's own words for this exact operation
spells.provenance: Simple Magic seed spell. Scald with the sign flipped and the target turned inward, which is the whole argument for signed magnitudes and a data-driven target shape: mending and harming were never two systems. SELF because canon's own instance of this operation is Gerik healing his OWN arm.

spells.canonAnchor: "'Magic' can be expressed as unnatural intelligence, or in strength, or reflexes" (L98) - the founding line for untrained magic, and its three named expressions ARE the three attributes
spells.provenance: Simple Magic seed spell, the STAT axis. One point of AGI for a quarter-hour. Because the whole game reads attributes through one function, this is felt in the shove contest, the lift, the cast, the cull and the next crafting - the standing Morrowind steer, taken literally.

spells.canonAnchor: L98's 'in strength'; Ignis's flesh magic is canon's worked example of self-tuning physiology (WorldBible section 3.2)
spells.provenance: Simple Magic seed spell. Same row as Steady the Hand with one word changed - the param field is the whole difference between two spells.

Simple Magic seed spell. The one crafting that feeds itself: WIT governs the linkcraft check, so a cleared head makes the next link likelier. Bounded by the same cost model as everything else, and priced highest of the three nudges for exactly that reason.

spells.canonAnchor: the same tuning turned outward; L98's three expressions with the sign reversed
spells.provenance: Simple Magic seed spell, the deepest thing on the public shelf. Taking a point off somebody else's reflexes is dearer than lending yourself one, and the raws say so only through baseResist - no code knows this spell is unkind.

notes: THE SPELL LIST IS DATA. Every crafting here is (effect x magnitude x duration x chance x area) and nothing else, so a tenth spell is a tenth row - no Java, no enum, no table. Nothing clamps magnitude: SpellCost prices what a crafting moves and how far, and the linkcraft check does the rest, which is why a spell nobody has reviewed cannot be accidentally strong. Note what is NOT here: every entry is SELF or TOUCH. Canon gates the unbridged link behind 'the gift' ('almost nobody can do this', L459), so the vocabulary supports RANGED and the public shelf does not teach it. canonAnchor/provenance/notes are documentation-only and ignored by the loader.
